heroHeadline: IRGC Fires Ballistic Missile at Kuwait (Intercepted); CENTCOM Destroys 2 IRGC Mine-Laying Vessels in Hormuz; Axios Reports 60-Day MoU Reached, Pending Trump; Diplomat Downplays — Day 90
heroSubtitle: Day 90 (May 28, 2026): The ceasefire framework faced its most severe test yet as military escalation accelerated on multiple fronts. The IRGC fired a ballistic missile at Kuwait City — the first Iranian strike on a Gulf capital since Day 70 (May 8) — which Kuwait's air defenses intercepted. CENTCOM called it an 'egregious ceasefire violation,' the strongest post-ceasefire language used to date. Separately, CENTCOM destroyed two IRGC mine-laying vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and intercepted multiple one-way attack drones after Iran fired on four merchant vessels attempting transit. The IRGC warned of 'full retaliation.' On the diplomatic front, Axios reported that US and Iranian negotiators had reached substantive agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to end the war, pending Trump's approval — but a senior mediating diplomat told the Times of Israel that the Axios framing 'mischaracterizes the state of negotiations,' with both sides still working toward agreement on outstanding issues. Israel struck southern Lebanon on Day 90, killing 14+ in drone strikes including 4 children in Adloun — and formally declared all territory south of the Zahrani River (~40km from the Israeli border) a 'combat zone.' Lebanon's cumulative death toll rose to 3,118+. Lebanon-Israel security talks in Washington were scheduled for May 29, with the critical June 2–3 Doha round remaining the last diplomatic gate before the ceasefire framework could formally collapse.
